newsitem.title: USA: Lawyers for Nichols say client "used" by McVeigh.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers for Nichols say client "used" by McVeigh.

text.p: Lawyers for accused Oklahoma City bombing co-defendant Terry Nichols said Monday their client was a victim of convicted bomber Timothy McVeigh.

In an interview with CBS News, attorneys Michael Tigar and Ronald Woods said their defence for Nichols was that he was unwittingly used by McVeigh in preparations for the April 19, 1995, explosion that killed 168 people and wounded more than 500.

"The evidence is going to be that Timothy McVeigh used Terry Nichols in much the same way that he used others," Tigar said in a CBS Evening News interview. He added that Nichols did not know what McVeigh was planning.
Prosecutors in McVeigh's trial said Nichols picked McVeigh up in Oklahoma City after McVeigh planted a getaway car there just before the attack.
Tigar said his client did indeed pick up McVeigh but he thought that his army buddy's car had broken down and he simply giving him a lift.
A jury sentenced McVeigh to death Friday after convicting him June 2 of the bombing.
Nichols, who has pleaded not guilty, is expected to go on trial in September. He faces the same 11 federal charges that McVeigh faced, including bombing and murder.
Nichols contends he was not at the scene of the blast and had nothing to do with it.
